outcome.answer:
This is already well-established in the graph, confirmed by human-authored notes with good confidence (0.8–0.85), so this isn't a new finding — it's a confirmed reading of existing evidence. Here's what's on record:

- **[[opt-suzuki-conditions]]** (optimization-campaign, confidence 0.85): best isolated yield was 76% at 1.5 mol% Pd/K₂CO₃/80 °C. The 100 °C run showed 79% by LCAP but only 68% isolated — explicitly attributed to protodeboronation. The note states plainly: "optimising on the wrong readout would have selected the hotter, worse condition."
- **[[failure-aqueous-protodeboronation]]** (failure-mode, confidence 0.8): confirms the mechanism — in THF/water at 100 °C, the boronic acid protodeboronates to benzene faster than it transmetalates, inflating LCAP conversion while isolated yield drops. This was "observed three times before it was recognised, because the assay looked better each time."
- That failure-mode note also **`contradicts`** [[bo-suzuki-next]] — flagging that the BO suggestion note proposes higher temperature because it was fitted on assay yield, not isolated yield, and never saw this failure mode.

Since you've confirmed this reading, I'll record it as a confirmed interaction so it's citable directly going forward instead of requiring you to re-derive it from the two notes each time.
